## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kathinuddhāra-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 30) governs the formal termination of the robe-making season (*kaṭhina*) within the nuns' community [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. The rule establishes that a nun who inappropriately hinders or obstructs the monastic community from ending the robe-making period commits an expiable offense (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. In the canonical origin narrative found at Vinaya IV 288, the nun Thullanandā prevents this legal procedure (*kammavācā*) from proceeding, an episode examined in Buddhaghosa's *Samantapāsādikā* (Sp 931) regarding valid and invalid grounds for terminating or delaying the *kaṭhina* privileges [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Full parallels are preserved in the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (pc 30) and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Pācittiya 30), as well as across other early Vinaya traditions in Chinese translation, including the Dharmaguptaka (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pc 109 and Pātimokkha Pc 109) and Sarvāstivāda (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pc 136 and Pātimokkha Pc 136) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies 644 text-reuse segments across 135 Pali works, sharing recurring legal and disciplinary formulae most heavily with Vinaya Khandhaka treatises—such as the *Senāsanakkhandhaka* (Kd 16), *Uposathakkhandhaka* (Kd 2), and *Cīvarakkhandhaka* (Kd 8)—as well as the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā*, *Vinayālaṅkāra-ṭīkā*, and other Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of this text with the Tibetan *Ekottarakarmaśataka* (D4118) [DharmaNexus].
